name: support
description: Golden support-question cases derived from the authly codebase (docs/how-to + docs/reference ground truth)

cases.name: invalid-email-or-password
cases.input: Login fails with AuthenticationError: invalid email or password. Which one is wrong?
cases.expected_output: The error never reveals which part failed: either no registered user matches the email or the password is wrong. Confirm the email exists via authly.users.list() and retry; remember only the first user created with a given email can match a login.

cases.name: client-valueerror-init
cases.input: Initializing the Authly client raises ValueError. Is that an AuthlyError?
cases.expected_output: No. ValueError from client construction is not an AuthlyError: it is a plain Python error meaning project_id or api_key was omitted or empty.

cases.name: list-for-user-never-raises
cases.input: Does permissions.list_for_user() raise for an unknown user ID?
cases.expected_output: No. permissions.list_for_user() never raises, even for unknown users; an unknown user simply has no assigned roles.

cases.name: revoke-idempotency
cases.input: If I revoke the same session twice, will the second call fail?
cases.expected_output: Revoking is idempotent in effect, but calling revoke() on a session that does not exist raises NotFoundError because revoke() performs a get() first.
